First, we evaluate the inner integral by integrating with respect to $x$, treating $y$ and $z$ as constants:    

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{2\pi }{\int }_{0}^{1}(x-y)^{2}+\operatorname{sin}⁡z\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{2\pi }[{\int }_{0}^{1}(x-y)^{2}+\operatorname{sin}⁡z\,\text{d}x]\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{2\pi }{[\frac{(x-y)^{3}}{3}]}_{x=0}^{x=1}+\operatorname{sin}⁡z[x]_{x=0}^{x=1}\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{2\pi }\frac{(1-y)^{3}}{3}-\frac{(0-y)^{3}}{3}+\operatorname{sin}⁡z(1-0)\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{2\pi }\frac{(1-y)^{3}+{y}^{3}}{3}+\operatorname{sin}⁡z\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we integrate with respect to $z$, treating $y$ as a constant: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1}[{\int }_{0}^{2\pi }\frac{(1-y)^{3}+{y}^{3}}{3}+\operatorname{sin}⁡z\,\text{d}z]\text{d}y & ={\int }_{0}^{1}[{\int }_{0}^{2\pi }\frac{(1-y)^{3}+{y}^{3}}{3}+\operatorname{sin}⁡z\,\text{d}z]\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}(\frac{(1-y)^{3}+{y}^{3}}{3}[z]_{z=0}^{z=2\pi }+[-\operatorname{cos}⁡z]_{z=0}^{z=2\pi })\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}(\frac{(1-y)^{3}+{y}^{3}}{3}(2\pi -0)+(-1+1))\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{2\pi }{3}{\int }_{0}^{1}(1-y)^{3}+{y}^{3}\text{d}y\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we integrate with respect to $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{2\pi }{3}{\int }_{0}^{1}(1-y)^{3}+{y}^{3}\text{d}y & =\frac{2\pi }{3}{[-\frac{(1-y)^{4}}{4}+\frac{{y}^{4}}{4}]}_{y=0}^{y=1} \\  & =\frac{2\pi }{3}((-0+\frac{1}{4})-(-\frac{1}{4}+0)) \\  & =\frac{2\pi }{3}\cdot \frac{1}{2} \\  & =\frac{\pi }{3}\end{aligned}
$$

First, we evaluate the inner integral by integrating with respect to $x$, treating $y$ and $z$ as constants:    

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{1}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{2}xy+yz+xz\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{1}^{2}[{\int }_{0}^{2}xy+yz+xz\,\text{d}x]\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{1}^{2}[{\int }_{0}^{2}(y+z)x+yz\,\text{d}x]\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{1}^{2}(y+z)\,{[\frac{{x}^{2}}{2}]}_{0}^{2}+yz[x]_{0}^{2}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{1}^{2}(y+z)(2-0)+yz(2-0)\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{1}^{2}2(y+z)+2yz\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we integrate with respect to $y$, treating $z$ as a constant: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{1}^{2}2(y+z)+2yz\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z & ={\int }_{0}^{1}[{\int }_{1}^{2}2(y+z)+2yz\,\text{d}y]\text{d}z \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}[{\int }_{1}^{2}2(1+z)y+2z\,\text{d}y]\text{d}z \\  & =2{\int }_{0}^{1}((1+z)[{y}^{2}]_{1}^{2}+2z[y]_{1}^{2})\,\text{d}z \\  & =2{\int }_{0}^{1}((1+z)(4-1)+2z(2-1))\text{d}z \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}(3(1+z)+2z)\text{d}z \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}(3+5z)\text{d}z\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1}(3+5z)\text{d}z & ={[3z+\frac{5}{2}{z}^{2}]}_{0}^{1} \\  & =3(1-0)+\frac{5}{2}(1-0) \\  & =\frac{11}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

First, we apply the sum rule and write our repeated integral as follows:

$$
{\int }_{-1}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{1}{x}^{2}\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z+{\int }_{-1}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{1}{y}^{2}\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z
$$

Since the domain of integration $R=[0,1]\times [0,2]\times [-1,1]$ is a rectangular box, and each integrand can be expressed as $f(x)\cdot g(y)\cdot h(z),$ we can rewrite our sum of repeated integrals as follows:

$$
{\int }_{0}^{1}{x}^{2}\,\text{d}x{\int }_{0}^{2}\,\text{d}y\,{\int }_{-1}^{1}\text{d}z\,+\,{\int }_{0}^{1}\,\text{d}x{\int }_{0}^{2}{y}^{2}\,\text{d}y\,{\int }_{-1}^{1}\text{d}z

Let's evaluate each of these separately:

- For the first product, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1}{x}^{2}\,\text{d}x{\int }_{0}^{2}\,\text{d}y\,{\int }_{-1}^{1}\text{d}z & ={[\frac{1}{3}{x}^{3}]}_{0}^{1}\cdot (2-0)\cdot (1-(-1)) \\  & =\frac{1}{3}\cdot 2\cdot 2 \\  & =\frac{4}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1}\,\text{d}x{\int }_{0}^{2}{y}^{2}\,\text{d}y\,{\int }_{-1}^{1}\text{d}z & =(1-0)\cdot {[\frac{1}{3}{y}^{3}]}_{0}^{2}\cdot (1-(-1)) \\  & =1\cdot \frac{8}{3}\cdot 2 \\  & =\frac{16}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we conclude that

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-1}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{1}{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z=\frac{4}{3}+\frac{16}{3}=\frac{20}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

$$

$$

$$

Since the domain of integration $R=[0,4]\times [1,2]\times [0,1]$ is a rectangular box, and each integrand can be expressed as $f(x)\cdot g(y)\cdot h(z),$ we can rewrite our sum of repeated integrals as follows:

$$
{\int }_{0}^{4}x\,\text{d}x{\int }_{1}^{2}{y}^{2}\,\text{d}y\,{\int }_{0}^{1}{z}^{3}\,\text{d}z-{\int }_{0}^{4}\text{d}x{\int }_{1}^{2}\text{d}y\,{\int }_{0}^{1}z\,\text{d}z
$$

Let's evaluate each of these separately:

- For the first product, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{4}x\,\text{d}x{\int }_{1}^{2}{y}^{2}\,\text{d}y\,{\int }_{0}^{1}{z}^{3}\,\text{d}z & ={[\frac{1}{2}{x}^{2}]}_{0}^{4}\cdot {[\frac{1}{3}{y}^{3}]}_{1}^{2}\cdot {[\frac{1}{4}{z}^{4}]}_{0}^{1} \\  & =(8-0)(\frac{8}{3}-\frac{1}{3})(\frac{1}{4}-0) \\  & =8(\frac{7}{3})(\frac{1}{4}) \\  & =\frac{14}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

- For the second product, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{4}\text{d}x{\int }_{1}^{2}\text{d}y\,{\int }_{0}^{1}z\,\text{d}z & =(4-0)\cdot (2-1)\cdot {[\frac{1}{2}{z}^{2}]}_{0}^{1} \\  & =4\cdot 1\cdot \frac{1}{2} \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we conclude that

$$

$$

Let's evaluate each of these separately:

- For the first product, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1}\text{d}x{\int }_{1}^{2}3{y}^{2}\,\text{d}y{\int }_{2}^{5}\text{d}z & =(1-0)\cdot [{y}^{3}]_{1}^{2}\cdot (5-2) \\  & =1\cdot (8-1)\cdot 3 \\  & =3\cdot 7 \\  & =21.\end{aligned}
$$

- For the second product, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1}4x\,\text{d}x{\int }_{1}^{2}\text{d}y{\int }_{2}^{5}\text{d}z & =[2{x}^{2}]_{0}^{1}\cdot (2-1)\cdot (5-2) \\  & =2\cdot 1\cdot 3 \\  & =6.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we conclude that

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{2}^{5}{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{1}^{2}(3{y}^{2}-1)\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}z=21-6=15.\end{aligned}
$$

$$
{\int }_{-1}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{1}3{x}^{2}\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z-{\int }_{-1}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{1}4{y}^{3}\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z-{\int }_{-1}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{1}2z\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z
$$

Since the domain of integration $R=[0,1]\times [0,2]\times [-1,1]$ is a rectangular box, and each integrand can be expressed as $f(x)\cdot g(y)\cdot h(z),$ we can rewrite our sum of repeated integrals as follows:

$$
{\int }_{0}^{1}3{x}^{2}\,\text{d}x{\int }_{0}^{2}\text{d}y{\int }_{-1}^{1}\text{d}z-{\int }_{0}^{1}\text{d}x{\int }_{0}^{2}4{y}^{3}\,\text{d}y{\int }_{-1}^{1}\text{d}z-{\int }_{0}^{1}\text{d}x{\int }_{0}^{2}\text{d}y{\int }_{-1}^{1}2z\,\text{d}z
$$

Let's evaluate each of these separately:

- For the first product, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1}3{x}^{2}\,\text{d}x{\int }_{0}^{2}\text{d}y{\int }_{-1}^{1}\text{d}z & =[{x}^{3}]_{0}^{1}\cdot (2-0)\cdot (1-(-1)) \\  & =1\cdot 2\cdot 2 \\  & =4.\end{aligned}
$$

- For the second product, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1}\text{d}x{\int }_{0}^{2}4{y}^{3}\,\text{d}y{\int }_{-1}^{1}\text{d}z & =(1-0)\cdot [{y}^{4}]_{0}^{2}\cdot (1-(-1)) \\  & =1\cdot 16\cdot 2 \\  & =32.\end{aligned}
$$

- For the third product, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1}\text{d}x{\int }_{0}^{2}\text{d}y{\int }_{-1}^{1}2z\,\text{d}z & =(1-0)\cdot (2-0)\cdot [{z}^{2}]_{-1}^{1} \\  & =1\cdot 2\cdot 0 \\  & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we conclude that

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-1}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{1}(3{x}^{2}-4{y}^{3}-2z)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z=4-32-0=-28.\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1}^{2}{\int }_{-1}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{1}{x}^{2}y+x{z}^{2}\,dz\,dx\,dy & ={\int }_{1}^{2}{\int }_{-1}^{2}[{\int }_{0}^{1}{x}^{2}y+x{z}^{2}\,dz]dx\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{2}{\int }_{-1}^{2}{[{x}^{2}yz+\frac{x{z}^{3}}{3}]}_{z=0}^{z=1}\,dx\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{2}{\int }_{-1}^{2}{x}^{2}y(1-0)+x(\frac{1}{3}-0)\,dx\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{2}{\int }_{-1}^{2}{x}^{2}y+\frac{1}{3}x\,dx\,dy\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we evaluate the inner integral by integrating with respect to $x$, treating $y$ as a constant: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1}^{2}{\int }_{-1}^{2}{x}^{2}y+\frac{1}{3}x\,dx\,dy & ={\int }_{1}^{2}[{\int }_{-1}^{2}{x}^{2}y+\frac{1}{3}x\,dx]dy \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{2}{[\frac{1}{3}{x}^{3}y+\frac{1}{6}{x}^{2}]}_{x=-1}^{x=2}\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{2}\frac{1}{3}y({2}^{3}-(-1)^{3})+\frac{1}{6}({2}^{2}-(-1)^{2}))\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{2}3y+\frac{1}{2}\,dy\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we integrate with respect to $y{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1}^{2}3y+\frac{1}{2}\,dx & ={[\frac{3{y}^{2}}{2}+\frac{y}{2}]}_{y=1}^{y=2} \\  & =(6+1)-(\frac{3}{2}+\frac{1}{2}) \\  & =5\end{aligned}
$$

canonical_examples.worked_solution:
First, we evaluate the inner integral by integrating with respect to $z,$ treating $x$ and $y$ as constants: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{x}{\int }_{0}^{3-x-y}x\,dz\,dy\,dx & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{x}[{\int }_{0}^{3-x-y}x\,dz]dy\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{x}x\cdot [z]_{z=0}^{z=3-x-y}\,dy\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{x}x(3-x-y)\,dy\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{x}3x-{x}^{2}-xy\,dy\,dx\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we evaluate the inner integral by integrating with respect to $y,$ treating $x$ as a constant: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{x}3x-{x}^{2}-xy\,dy\,dx & ={\int }_{0}^{2}[{\int }_{0}^{x}3x-{x}^{2}-xy\,dy]dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{[(3x-{x}^{2})y-\frac{1}{2}x{y}^{2}]}_{y=0}^{y=x}\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}(3x-{x}^{2})(x-0)-\frac{1}{2}x({x}^{2}-0)\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}3{x}^{2}-{x}^{3}-\frac{1}{2}{x}^{3}\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}3{x}^{2}-\frac{3}{2}{x}^{3}\,dx\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we integrate with respect to $x{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{2}3{x}^{2}-\frac{3}{2}{x}^{3}\,dx & ={[{x}^{3}-\frac{3}{8}{x}^{4}]}_{x=0}^{x=2} \\  & =8-6 \\  & =2\end{aligned}
$$

Since the domain of integration $R = [1,2] \times \left[0,\pi/2\right] \times [1,4]$ is a rectangular box and the integrand can be expressed as $f(x)\cdot g(y)\cdot h(z),$ we can rewrite our repeated integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}{\int }_{1}^{4}\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡y}{x}\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{1}^{2}\frac{dx}{x}{\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}\operatorname{sin}⁡y\,dy{\int }_{1}^{4}dz\end{aligned}
$$

Evaluating each integral separately, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1}^{2}\frac{1}{x}\,dx{\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}\operatorname{sin}⁡y\,dy\,{\int }_{1}^{4}dz & =[\operatorname{ln}⁡|x|]_{1}^{2}\cdot [-\operatorname{cos}⁡y]_{0}^{\pi /2}\cdot (4-1) \\  & =(\operatorname{ln}⁡2-\operatorname{ln}⁡1)\cdot (-\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2})+\operatorname{cos}⁡(0))\cdot 3 \\  & =(\operatorname{ln}⁡2-0)\cdot (0+1)\cdot 3 \\  & =3\operatorname{ln}⁡2.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we conclude that

$$
\int_{1}^{2}\int_{0}^{\pi/2} \int_{1}^{4} \dfrac{\sin{y}}{x} \: \textrm{d}z \: \textrm{d}y \: \textrm{d}x = 3\ln 2.
$$
